docker.title: Docker labels
docker.intro: PROXY64 creates proxy hosts from the labels of your containers. Name, scheme and target come from the labels, everything else is set on the host and survives container updates.
docker.on_hint: Containers with node64.proxy.host become proxy hosts. When a container (or the label) is removed, PROXY64 deletes the host after 2 minutes, including its CDN64 online registration.
docker.traefik_hint: Takes over Host(…) rules, port, scheme and traefik.docker.network, but no middlewares, path rules or tls.certresolver. Own node64 labels take precedence.
docker.host_hint: Empty = default (like Docker monitoring). Allowed: unix:///path, tcp://host:port or http(s)://host:port, e.g. a docker-socket-proxy. Only the Docker host Node64 runs on.
docker.cert_none: Don't request one (matching existing certificate, otherwise HTTP only)
docker.cert_hint: For newly created Docker hosts PROXY64 requests a certificate this way. Without a choice the host uses a matching existing certificate (e.g. wildcard), otherwise it stays on HTTP.
docker.tos_hint: Once here instead of per container; applies to all Let's Encrypt certificates.
docker.error_hint: Is the socket mounted and readable (group_add)? With docker-socket-proxy set CONTAINERS=1 and EVENTS=1. Until then PROXY64 deletes no hosts.
docker.off_hint: Switched off. Switch on so PROXY64 reads the containers.
docker.empty: No container with node64.proxy.* or Traefik labels found.
docker.form_hint: Comes from the Docker labels of container {name}.
docker.form_access: Comes from the Docker label (access list "{name}").
docker.ignored: Skipped (does not affect access): {name}. If one of them sets security headers (e.g. from a file), add them to the host under “Advanced”.
docker.form_locked: Names, scheme and target are therefore locked; everything else can be set here and is kept.
docker.help_labels: Put labels on the container, PROXY64 creates the host by itself:
docker.help_network: Network: Node64 and the container need a shared Docker network (or Node64 in host network mode); with several networks set node64.proxy.network.
docker.help_socket: Socket: mount /var/run/docker.sock read-only (with group_add) or use a docker-socket-proxy with CONTAINERS=1 and EVENTS=1.

f.names_hint: One per line (or comma separated), wildcards like *.example.ipv64.de too. The DNS record must point to this connection.
f.target_hint: The service in your home network, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8123. The target gets the name the visitor used plus X-Forwarded-For/-Proto/-Host and X-Real-IP.
f.verify_target_hint: Off: self-signed certificates (Proxmox, UniFi, NAS) work too – like NPM.
f.cache_assets_hint: Keep images, CSS, JS and fonts in memory.
f.limits_on: Overload protection active: limits per IP address (connections, requests), ban on sustained floods and a slot limit at the target
f.block_exploits_hint: Reject typical attacks (SQL and file injection, path traversal, Log4Shell, .git/.env) with 403. Sign-ins via OAuth/OIDC (e.g. Home Assistant, Keycloak, Authelia) and WebDAV stay allowed; addresses on the allow list are exempt.
f.websockets_hint: For services with live connections (e.g. Home Assistant).
f.probe: Check whether the target is reachable
f.probe_hint: Off for targets without a web interface (e.g. a database behind TLS passthrough): no “unreachable” badge and no metric for this target.
f.cert_hint: Certificates come from the certificate manager (Let's Encrypt via ipv64 or your own). Without a matching certificate the browser shows a warning.
f.force_ssl_hint: Requests via http:// are redirected to https://.
f.hsts_hint: Browsers use only HTTPS for this domain for two years.
f.http3_hint: Needs 443/UDP on the router and the switch in the common entrance.
f.min_tls_hint: TLS 1.3 is current; 1.2 for older devices. BSI: only methods per the technical guideline (version 2026-01).
f.cert_new: Request a new certificate right away
f.cert_new_hint: For all domains of this host; the request runs in the background after saving.
f.cert_tos_hint: For certificates the node creates one Let’s Encrypt account; accept the terms of service for it. Contact e-mail (optional) under
f.redirect_hint: Domain, optionally with port and path (e.g. www.example.com/new). "Same as request" uses http or https as the visitor came.
f.dead_hint: This host answers every request with a neutral "404" page. With a certificate also via HTTPS.
f.stream_hint: Just the name, without a target: switch it on in CDN64 (mode 1) and pick it in the stream under “Reachable from the internet via CDN64”. Nothing answers on 80/443 under this name.
f.pass_hint: The connection is handed raw to this target by name, without decrypting it here – the target needs its own certificate. Port 80 redirects to HTTPS.
f.pass_bw_hint: Bandwidth for all connections of this name together, empty or 0 = unlimited. Above it traffic is throttled, not cut. Also applies via CDN64.
f.access_hint: Access only with password and/or from certain networks.
f.geo_hint: Country codes, e.g. DE, AT, CH; EU stands for the 27 EU member states. Private networks and the allow list are never blocked.
f.locations_hint: Paths with their own target, e.g. /api to another service. The longest matching path wins; everything else goes to the host's target.
f.locations_more: Empty rows are ignored. For more locations save and edit again.
f.loc_deny_ph: empty = error page, e.g. / or https://vault.example.com/
f.loc_deny_hint: If the access list of this location denies a visitor (e.g. /admin only from the LAN), they get a redirect (302) there instead of the error page; allowed visitors still get through. Relative path (/…) or http(s) address. If the list asks for a login, the login stays.
f.target_path_hint: Put in front of every request, e.g. /rezepte: /soup becomes /rezepte/soup at the target. The address in the browser stays, redirects and cookie paths of the target are written back. Empty = unchanged.
f.loc_action_hint: Block: error page with status 400–499 (default 403). Fixed response: status 200–599 (default 200), content at most 64 KB, e.g. the mta-sts.txt. Neither needs a target.
f.loc_adv_hint: Empty = same as host. Upload -1 = unlimited. Headers apply in addition to those of the host, same name: the location wins. Example: /Microsoft-Server-ActiveSync with a timeout of 3650 s and without buffering.
f.only_locations_hint: PROXY64 answers every other path with 404 and never asks the target of the host – e.g. mta-sts, autodiscover and autoconfig of mailcow with only the one file they need.
f.adv_headers_hint: One "Name: value" or name per line. Connection headers (Connection, Upgrade, Content-Length …) cannot be changed.
f.adv_gzip: Compress responses (zstd, Brotli, gzip – depending on the browser)
f.adv_limits_hint: Timeout: how long to wait for the target's answer, 0 = no limit. Upload: larger requests get 413, 0 = unlimited.
f.target_http_hint: Automatic: HTTP/2 for https targets that offer it, otherwise HTTP/1.1. HTTP/1.1 only for problems with NTLM/Exchange. h2c for cleartext gRPC services such as NetBird (for https targets: HTTP/2 only). WebSockets always use HTTP/1.1.
f.proxy_protocol_hint: Sends the real visitor address to the target (like HAProxy send-proxy), also via CDN64. Only switch it on if the target expects the PROXY protocol – e.g. Postfix/Dovecot (mailcow) or another reverse proxy; otherwise the target cannot understand the connection.
f.adv_bw_hint: Bandwidth for all visitors of this host together, empty or 0 = unlimited. Above it traffic is throttled, not cut. Also applies to WebSockets and via CDN64.
f.adv_trusted_hint: From these networks the IP in X-Forwarded-For (with Cloudflare also CF-Connecting-IP) counts as the real client IP. Otherwise the connection’s peer counts.
f.adv_access_log_hint: Every request individually under "Requests". The hourly counters always run.
f.adv_no_limits_hint: The per-IP request limit and the per-target limit do not apply to this host (e.g. an API used by many devices behind one address). Connection limits and bans still apply.
f.status_page_missing: Status page #{id} (does not exist on this node)
f.status_hc_off: The Healthchecks module is switched off. Until it runs, this host answers with 503.
f.status_page_hint: The page appears directly under "/" on this domain. If it is switched off, the host answers with 404.
f.ai_bots_user: Also block fetches on behalf of users (ChatGPT-User, Perplexity-User …)
f.ai_robots: Serve robots.txt that blocks AI bots
f.ai_hint: Requests from known AI crawlers (user agent list from ipv64.net) get 403, /robots.txt stays reachable. Their IP networks are also blocked by the “v64 AI bots (IP)” blocklist under Security.
f.cert_ways_hint: Greyed out ways need something first (API key, DNS account, own CA). Alias via ipv64 and all settings are under

acl.name: Name
acl.all_long: Both required: allowed IP and login (where set up)

acl.pass_auth_hint: Off: the target does not see the Authorization header.
acl.users_hint: New or changed users as "name:password", one per line. Passwords are stored hashed only (bcrypt).
acl.rules_hint: One "allow" or "deny" and an IP, a network or "all" per line. The first match counts, without a match access is denied. Dynamic: "self" = the node's own public IP (IPv4 and IPv6 /64; "self4"/"self6" only one of them – if DynDNS detects DS-Lite/CGNAT, "self" leaves out the IPv4, which many connections share) or a DNS name such as a DynDNS name (resolved again every minute, IPv6 as /64). This lets devices at home through without a password even via CDN64. If a name cannot be resolved, "deny" still applies.

hp.title: Honeypot64
hp.hint: PROXY64 can work together with the Honeypot64 module of this node. Each point can be switched on separately and is off by default.
hp.decoy_hint: Requests without a matching host (IP only, foreign domain, unknown name) go to the web decoy of Honeypot64 instead of the default page. Unknown names get the fallback certificate.
hp.decoy_missing: Honeypot64 does not offer a web decoy right now – until then the default page applies.
hp.decoy_visible: The node then answers unknown requests visibly (login page, fallback certificate) – even if the default page is set to “close connection”.
hp.access_hint: For each request only metadata goes to Honeypot64 (IP, host, method, path without query, status, failed login) – never content. The honeypot evaluates it with its own rules.
hp.access_missing: Honeypot64 does not evaluate accesses right now.
hp.block: Block attackers from the honeypot immediately
hp.block_hint: Attackers from the honeypot are blocked by PROXY64 at once for all hosts and streams. Never private addresses, the allow list or trusted proxies.
hp.block_wanted: Switched on by Honeypot64 ("Block detected attackers in PROXY64").

cdn64.c4_hint: Answers of the target with 4xx (e.g. not found, not logged in) – usually not an error, e.g. missing icons or expired logins.

localdns.title: Add to local DNS64

localdns.excluded: Not added (wildcard or main domain – DNS64 would also hide mail, TXT and other records there): {list}.

errpage.title: Custom error page
errpage.hint: Instead of the neutral error page, PROXY64 shows your HTML when the target is not reachable (502), overloaded (503) or not answering (504). Empty = neutral page.
errpage.html_hint: The whole page, at most 64 KB. {{STATUS}} is replaced by the status code, {{HOST}} by the name. Embed images and fonts (data:) – the target is not reachable then.
errpage.override: Also replace errors of the target (5xx)
errpage.override_hint: If the target itself answers with a 5xx error (e.g. app in maintenance mode), visitors see your page too; the status code stays. Applies on the node, also via CDN64 mode 1 and 2; if the node or the tunnel is down completely, the CDN64 server shows its own page.

maint.on_hint: The name stays reachable, visitors see a maintenance page instead of the target (HTTP 503 with Retry-After, never cached). Certificates keep renewing.
maint.html_hint: Only for “Custom HTML”: the whole page, max. 64 KB. Embed images and fonts (data:), the target is unreachable during maintenance.
maint.scope_hint: Applies to this host on the node, also via CDN64 mode 1 and 2. With CDN64 mode 3 the server goes straight to the target – maintenance mode has no effect there.

protection.head: What CDN64 blocked for you
protection.lead: CDN64 helps, protects you and takes you further: the CDN64 servers filter automated attacks, scanners and known attack tools before they reach your network.
protection.unavailable: The statistics from ipv64.net are not available right now.
protection.k_blocked_hint: Connections and requests that never reached your target: blocklists, access list, overload, WAF patterns and attack tools.
protection.k_ips_hint: Distinct blocked attacker addresses (IPv6 per /64), counted per report interval of the servers.
protection.k_overload_hint: Connections and requests over the limits: connections per IP, connection rate, request limit.
protection.k_hidden_hint: Connections via CDN64: visitors only see the CDN64 servers, not your IP address.
protection.chart_empty: Nothing was blocked in this period.
protection.nodata: No protection figures in this period yet. They appear once the CDN64 servers block something for your names.
protection.waf_mode1: WAF patterns only apply in mode 2 and 3 (in mode 1 the servers do not see the requests).
protection.tools_hint: Fingerprints (JA4) from the Honeypot64 database of ipv64.net, merged from all honeypots.
protection.tools_count: Start phase: tools are counted, not blocked yet.
protection.tools_empty: No known attack tool in this period.
protection.without_ip: Your IP address would have been visible {n} times.
protection.without_v4: {n} visitor connections came via IPv4 – with DS-Lite or IPv6 only, you would not be reachable for them otherwise.
protection.mode_1: Mode 1 (pass through): blocklists, access list, overload limits and known attack tools are kept away by the servers – without decrypting your connection.
protection.mode_2: Mode 2 (terminate on the servers): like mode 1, plus WAF patterns – requests for .env, .git, configuration files and typical scanners are rejected on the servers.
protection.mode_3: Mode 3 (direct to the target): blocklists, access list, overload limits, attack tools and WAF patterns – without Node64 in between.
protection.honest: CDN64 filters automated attacks and scanners, but not targeted attacks on your application – updates still matter.
protection.sw_hint: Applies to all names of the host. During the start phase ipv64 only counts attack tools, even with "block".

dnscheck.own_label: Additional resolvers for the check (one per line)
dnscheck.own_hint: IP address (port 53), IP:port or https://…, tls://…, quic://… (at most 10). They are added to the built-in resolvers and asked first. Empty = built-in only.

ports.title: Ports
ports.hint: Which ports Node64 uses or wants to use. A port can only be opened once per address; modules share 80 and 443 through the common entrance.
ports.edge_hint: Opens the ports only while a module needs them (e.g. PROXY64 or Let's Encrypt via HTTP-01). Forward 80 and 443 (TCP, for HTTP/3 also 443/UDP) on the router to this node.
ports.edge_decoy: Currently replaced by the honeypot decoy (PROXY64 › Access › Honeypot64). The setting here applies again as soon as the decoy is off or Honeypot64 is not running.
ports.edge_public_hint: Only needed if the router forwards a different port (e.g. 443 → 8443). Empty = same as HTTPS port.
ports.edge_pp_hint: If PROXY64 sits behind another proxy that only passes TCP or TLS through (e.g. Traefik with proxyProtocol, HAProxy send-proxy), enter its address or network here. Only from there Node64 reads a PROXY header (v1/v2) with the real visitor address on ports 80/443 – for access lists, logs, the honeypot and rate limits. Separate several with spaces or commas, empty = off. If the proxy terminates TLS itself and sends X-Forwarded-For, add it under “Trusted proxies in front” (Advanced) of the proxy host instead.
ports.err_port: Ports must be between 0 and 65535 (0 = off).
ports.ui_public: Also reachable from the internet (not recommended)
ports.ui_hint: The interface is then also reachable at https://<name>. Default: only from your own network, everyone else gets 404.
ports.ui_cert: Certificate of the web interface (HTTPS port and name at the entrance)
ports.ui_cert_auto: Automatic: matching certificate for the requested name, otherwise self-signed
ports.ui_cert_env: NODE64_TLS_CERT is set: the HTTPS port uses this file, the choice only applies to the name at the entrance.
ports.ui_cert_hint: Changes apply without restart. Certificates come from the central manager:
ports.page_hint: All ports Node64 uses or wants to use, what runs over the port of another part and which connections are outgoing. A port can be opened only once per address and protocol.
ports.open_missing_hint: Node64 reports the port as open, but nothing listens on it in the network namespace.
ports.open_unknown_hint: Whether a port is really open can only be checked on Linux (/proc/net).
ports.open_hint: “Really open?” checks whether Node64 listens on the port – not whether it is reachable from outside (Docker forwarding, router, firewall).
ports.foreign_hint: The port is open, but no part of Node64 opened it – another program in the same network (e.g. on the host with --network host) uses it.
ports.low_hint: Ports below 1024 need root, the capability cap_net_bind_service or a suitable net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start.
ports.low_denied: Port below 1024: Node64 is not allowed to open it.
ports.edge_ui_moved: Name and certificate of the interface are now under
ports.low_root: Node64 runs as root and may open all ports.
ports.low_cap: Node64 has the capability cap_net_bind_service and may open ports below 1024.
ports.low_sysctl: Ports from {n} are allowed without special rights (net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start).
ports.low_none: Node64 may not open ports below 1024 (neither root nor cap_net_bind_service).
ports.low_denied_hint: A port below 1024 cannot be opened: set --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE on the container or choose a port from 1024.
ports.low_unknown: Rights unknown (can only be checked on Linux).
ports.low_explain: The Node64 image sets cap_net_bind_service so that DNS (53), HTTP (80) and HTTPS (443) work without root; Docker usually allows all ports inside the container anyway.
ports.docker_title: Docker: port forwarding or host network
ports.docker_hint: With -p every port has to be forwarded separately, TCP and UDP apart (e.g. -p 53:53 -p 53:53/udp). New ports need a container restart.
ports.docker_args_hint: Forwardings for the configured ports (without local-only addresses).
ports.docker_host: With --network host (network_mode: host) the ports apply directly on the host; no other program may use them. Recommended for streams, DNS64 and Honeypot64.
ports.pub_yes_hint: Docker bridge network: a probe request via the Docker host reached PROXY64 – the port is published on the host.
ports.pub_no_hint: Docker bridge network: PROXY64 listens inside the container, but the port is not published on the Docker host.
ports.pub_title: PROXY64 is not reachable from outside: ports on the Docker host are missing
ports.pub_alert: Port {ports} is not published on the Docker host (gateway {gw}) – requests and Let’s Encrypt don’t arrive. Forward the port at start and recreate the container:
ports.pub_compose: docker compose – add to the service (docker-compose.yml):
ports.pub_host: Or start in host network mode (--network host); then no other program may use 80/443. If the port is published under another number (e.g. -p 8443:443), enter it under “External port”.
ports.open_bridge_hint: In a Docker bridge network Node64 additionally checks for PROXY64 whether the HTTP and HTTPS ports are published on the Docker host (probe request via the gateway).

cluster.title: Cluster
cluster.intro: Several nodes sync settings and entries directly, also across networks. You choose per module and area what is synced.
cluster.tls_hint: The connection is always encrypted; a self-signed certificate is enough.
cluster.apikey_hint: Warning: the API key gives full access to your ipv64 account and is sent to all nodes. It is only accepted with the same account or by nodes without a key.
cluster.node_settings_hint: Time zone, self-update (mode, channel, time window) and MCP on/off. Never synced: node name and ID, ports, addresses, certificates, cluster and network settings.
cluster.account_self: This node belongs to ipv64 account #{account}.
cluster.account_none: This node has no ipv64 account.
cluster.account_rule: All nodes of a cluster share the same ipv64 account or have none; two different accounts are never possible.
cluster.how_notify: If several nodes measure a check, exactly one notifies: the first reachable one in the list of measuring nodes. The check shows which one.
cluster.fwd_self: This node passes changes of nodes without Healthchecks sync on to ipv64.

reason.account_mismatch: The other node (now) belongs to a different ipv64 account. There is no communication with it until it is resumed.
reason.identity_changed: The key or ID of the other node has changed (e.g. reinstalled). There is no communication with it until it is resumed.
reason.tls_binding: The HTTPS connection is not bound to the pairing, e.g. because a proxy terminates it. Address the node directly via its HTTPS port.
reason.version_too_old: The other node is too old for the cluster. Please update Node64 there.

cluster.reason_unknown: The node is suspended until it is resumed.
cluster.areas_none: No area is switched on for syncing there.
cluster.areas_unknown: Older version: which areas are switched on there is unknown.
cluster.area_off_here: Off on this node – not synced.
cluster.remove_confirm: Remove “{name}” from the cluster? All nodes of the cluster are told.
cluster.empty: No other nodes yet. Create a code on one node and join with it on the other.
cluster.sync_hint: The switches apply to the whole cluster: whatever you switch on or off here, all nodes adopt automatically (nodes with an older version keep their own switches). An area is only exchanged with nodes that have it switched on as well.
cluster.channels_hint: Only needed without a connection to ipv64.net – linked nodes get the portal's channels via ipv64.net. Only the node's own channels are synced, never those of the portal.
cluster.dyndns_hint: Only one node reports the addresses to ipv64 (preferred node on the DynDNS page). If it fails, another one takes over – in a different network the names then point to its connection.
cluster.users_hint: Users with the same name that differ (e.g. another password) are never overwritten: they are offered for choice on this page. The last user of a node is never deleted.
cluster.users_title: Users in the cluster: please choose
cluster.users_choose_hint: Users with the same name differ (e.g. password or 2FA). Until you choose, each node keeps its own; the chosen version then applies to the whole cluster.
cluster.users_confirm: Use this version of the user for the whole cluster? The other versions are replaced.
cluster.users_chosen: User chosen, the other nodes take it over.
cluster.users_unknown: This version is no longer up for choice.

link.key_or: Or with a code on the website:

link.key_failed: Linking with the API key failed: {err}
link.already_linked: This node is already linked to ipv64.

link.key_mismatch: The ipv64 API key in the settings belongs to a different account ({account}, #{key}) than this link (#{link}). DynDNS and healthchecks then run under different accounts.
link.peers_hint: Known via the ipv64 hub servers. Nodes do not connect to each other directly; a check can be measured by several nodes.
link.title: Healthchecks sync with ipv64
link.unavailable: Linking is not available in this installation.
link.local_notifications: Also send my own channels locally while linked

link.unlink_confirm: Unlink? The node keeps running standalone.
link.keep_checks: Keep the {count} checks measured only by this node running at ipv64 as online checks (within the limit). Unchecked, they are deleted at ipv64.
link.scope: Only these {own} checks are affected. The other {other} checks in the account (from other nodes or online checks) stay at ipv64 in any case.
link.code_intro: Enter this code at ipv64.net. It is valid for 10 minutes.
link.step2: Enter the code, choose location and remote management
link.waiting: Waiting for the code to be entered at ipv64.net …

link.rejected_old: Rejected before the node could store the reason. “Send again” shows the reason and the ipv64 state.
link.keep_server_hint: Discard the local change and take the ipv64 state here.
link.keep_local_hint: Send the local version to ipv64 once more (e.g. after fixing the reason).
link.keep_ignore_hint: The local version stays on this node but is no longer sent to ipv64 (until the next change).
link.delete_here_hint: ipv64 does not have this entry – delete it on this node too.
link.delete_here_confirm: Delete the entry on this node? ipv64 does not have it.

dhcp.title: DHCP server
dhcp.hint_off: The DHCP server hands out IP addresses to the devices on your network and sets this node as their DNS server. It is off and uses no port. Add a network first, then start the dry run.
dhcp.hint_observe: Dry run: the DHCP server only listens and never answers. Under “Recent requests” you see which devices ask and which address they would get. Other DHCP servers on the network are reported.
dhcp.hint_on: The DHCP server hands out addresses. There must be no second DHCP server on the network – turn off the one in your router.
dhcp.no_scope: Nothing is running yet: add a network and enable it.
dhcp.on_confirm: Turn on the DHCP server? It hands out addresses right away. Turn off your router's DHCP server first, otherwise devices get conflicting addresses.
dhcp.bridge: DHCP needs the host network (or macvlan): in the Docker bridge network the devices' requests do not arrive. Start the container with:
dhcp.foreign: Another DHCP server found on the network: {server} ({net}, last seen {time}). Turn it off before you enable DHCP here.
dhcp.iface_hint: Network card or VLAN of the host, e.g. eth0 or eth0.20. One network per interface.
dhcp.range_hint: Devices get their address from this range. Fixed addresses may also lie outside it.
dhcp.name: Label
dhcp.dns_hint: Empty = this node (recommended), in a cluster also the other nodes in this network. Separate several with commas.
dhcp.authoritative_hint: If a device asks for an address that does not fit here, the server declines so the device gets a new one right away (important when switching from the router).
dhcp.pxe_hint: Only for devices that boot from the network (e.g. netboot.xyz). Leave empty if you do not need it.
dhcp.err_iface: The interface {iface} does not exist on this host.
dhcp.err_addr: The node has no address in network {net} on {iface}. Give the host a fixed IPv4 address there.
dhcp.err_listen: Port 67 cannot be opened (is a DHCP server already running on the host?): {err}
dhcp.scope_delete_confirm: Delete network {name} with all fixed addresses and leases?
dhcp.release_confirm: Release address {ip}? It is free again right away; the device gets an address at its next renewal at the latest.
dhcp.res_ip_hint: Must be in the network, ideally outside the address range.
dhcp.no_reservations: No fixed addresses yet. Tip: in the leased addresses, the pin turns an address into a fixed one with one click.
dhcp.role_hint: The standby node only hands out addresses when the primary node is really gone. Turn on the areas “DHCP networks” and “DHCP leases” in the cluster on both nodes.
dhcp.reserve_alone: Standby node without a primary node for its networks: it stays silent until a primary node with this network is known (turn on the area “DHCP networks” in the cluster on both nodes).
dhcp.reserve_standby: Standby node: {nodes} is reachable – this node does not answer.
dhcp.reserve_active: Standby node: {nodes} is not reachable – this node is handing out the addresses now.
dhcp.relay_hint: For networks the node does not reach directly (e.g. a VLAN behind the router): the router forwards the requests to the node as a DHCP relay.
dhcp.domain_hint: Devices get names like laptop.home.lan – from the fixed address or from the device itself.
dhcp.group_hint: Adds the MAC to the group – its rules then apply even if the IP changes.
dhcp.no_iface: Taken over from the cluster: choose the interface and enable the network.
dhcp.two_primary: Two DHCP servers: in network {net}, {nodes} also hands out addresses as primary node. Set one of the nodes to “Standby node”.

ra.title: IPv6: DNS via router advertisement
ra.hint: Announces this node as DNS server via IPv6 (RDNSS, also works on Android). Node64 is not a router here: addresses from your provider's prefix and the route to the internet still come from the router. Independent of the DHCP server; every node in the cluster announces itself.
ra.no_addr_short: no ULA or global IPv6 address
ra.domain_hint: Search domain for the devices (DNSSL), e.g. home.lan – empty = none.
ra.err_self_router: A router service on this host (radvd, odhcpd) already announces on the interface – Node64 does not send its own RAs here (they would remove the default route from the devices). Please add DNS in the router service (RDNSS).
ra.err_no_addr: No IPv6 address to announce – or DNS64 does not answer via IPv6 on port 53 (port or bind address)
ra.err_socket: Router advertisements cannot be sent: {err}. The container needs host network and cap_net_raw.
ra.no_routers: No router has answered. “Check network” asks the routers (router solicitation).
ra.no_addrs: No router hands out IPv6 addresses in this network (no prefix with SLAAC, no DHCPv6). Without an address the announced DNS server is of no use to the devices – turn on IPv6 in the router.
ra.other_dns: The router {router} announces its own DNS server ({dns}). Devices then also ask there, blocking and local names do not work reliably. In the router, set the DNSv6 server for the home network to this node (FRITZ!Box: Home Network → Network → Network Settings → IPv6 Settings).

pub.refused: {n} queries from networks not allowed were rejected (last {ip}, {time}). If the network is yours, add it under “Additional allowed client networks”.
pub.missing: Docker bridge network: DNS64 listens inside the container, but these ports do not arrive via the Docker host – probably not published: {ports}. If they are in docker run or compose, the host firewall (e.g. ufw) often blocks the path from the container to the host that the node checks – then this notice does not apply.
pub.host: Alternatively network_mode: host – then nothing needs to be published, and DNS64 sees the real device addresses.
pub.gateway: The log shows the Docker gateway {gw} instead of the device IP. Real client IPs (and device groups) are only available with network_mode: host.
pub.anon_mask: "Client addresses in the log" is set to "shortened": devices in the same network appear with the same shortened address (Settings).
pub.anon_hide: "Client addresses in the log" is set to "do not store": no client address is in the log (Settings).

zones.settings: Zone settings (authoritative, device names, TTL, SOA, dynamic updates)
zones.delete_confirm: Delete zone "{name}"? The records stay (under "Without zone").
zones.dynamic_hint: DHCP servers like pfSense, OPNsense or Kea register device names themselves (A, AAAA, PTR, TXT, DHCID …).
zones.tsig_renew_confirm: Create a new key? The old one stops working immediately.

zones.name: Zone
zones.auth_hint: Otherwise names DNS64 does not know go on to forwarding and the router.

forwards.title: Forwarding
forwards.domain_hint: Applies to all names below, e.g. company.local, corp.example.com or a network like 192.168.0.0/16 (becomes the reverse zone).
forwards.servers_hint: One per line: IP (port 53), IP:port, tls://…, https://…/dns-query or quic://…; in order, the next one on failure.
forwards.test: Test (query the SOA of the domain)
forwards.builtin: Local names (.lan, .local, .fritz.box …) and private reverse lookups
forwards.order: Order: custom records, rewrites, forwards, router, internet. If none of the servers answers, the result is SERVFAIL – the name never goes to the internet.
forwards.rw_hint: DNS64 resolves the target itself and answers under the queried name (without CNAME). *.example.com applies to all names below.

dns64.title: DNS64
dns64.not_running: The DNS service is not running.

lists.title: Blocklists
lists.hint: Tick and apply; the DNS service then reloads the lists. “Domains” only counts entries not already in a list above.
lists.add_hint: Formats: hosts file, one domain per line or Adblock syntax (||domain^, exceptions @@||domain^; with a single bar |domain^ or @@|domain^ exactly this name).
lists.hint_categories: “Child protection” and “Bypass” apply to all devices; “Bypass” blocks foreign DoH servers, VPNs and proxies. Stronger levels sometimes block wanted sites too – then allow the domain.
lists.bulk_hint: Several lists at once: one URL per line, optionally with a name in front (“Name | URL”).

allow.title: Allowed domains
allow.not_running: The allowlist can be edited once the DNS service is running.
allow.import_hint: One domain per line, e.g. from the allowlist.txt of the old DNS64 container or a Pi-hole whitelist. Comments (#) and timestamps are ignored, existing entries stay.

up.title: Upstream servers
up.hint: Queries to the internet go encrypted to the configured servers (DoH, DoT or DoQ).

cache.title: DNS cache
cache.hint: Popular domains are renewed shortly before they expire. Expired entries are served instantly for up to 1 hour and refreshed in the background.

top.title: Top lists
top.all_title: Full list with pages, search and sorting

settings.firefox_canary: Firefox uses DNS64 (switch off Firefox’s own DoH)
settings.firefox_canary_hint: DNS64 does not resolve use-application-dns.net; Firefox then switches off its built-in DoH and asks DNS64 – otherwise Firefox bypasses blocklists and groups. On by default, like Pi-hole.
settings.title: Settings
settings.bind_one: Fixed address: DNS64 only listens on this one address. Devices of the other IP family (e.g. IPv6 clients with an IPv4 address) then get no DNS; leave empty for IPv4 and IPv6.
settings.port_hint: UDP and TCP. Devices on your network use this host's IP as DNS server, which only works with port 53. Other ports are for testing or when 53 is taken.
settings.router_none: No router found at the moment, local names are not resolved.
settings.router_hint: Names like fritz.box or .lan only go to this server, never to the internet. IPv4 or IPv6, optionally with port. Automatic: the gateway.
settings.router_domains: Detected router suffix: {list} (goes to the router like .lan).
settings.mdns: Resolve .local names and device names via mDNS in your own network
settings.mdns_hint: DNS64 asks the devices themselves for names like printer.local and passes them on as normal DNS – also to devices in other networks and in the VPN. DNS64 also learns the router's own suffix (e.g. .home-net). Only works if Node64 is directly in the LAN (host network or macvlan).
settings.docker_hint: Containers with the label node64.dns.name (names, comma) get own records in DNS64, on this node only. Address: label node64.dns.ip (addresses, or “container” for the container’s address with macvlan/ipvlan), otherwise the address below or the node’s LAN address. Synced every minute; when a container disappears, its records go after two minutes.
settings.docker_none: No containers with the label node64.dns.name.
settings.docker_err_no_ip: no address – set the label node64.dns.ip or enter an address above (in the Docker bridge network Node64 does not know the host’s address)
settings.mdns_none: No device answers at the moment – is Node64 behind the Docker bridge?
settings.anonymize_hint: Shortened or not stored applies to new entries; device names and top clients are then limited or unavailable.
settings.allow_nets_hint: Private networks and Tailscale are always allowed. Add further networks here, e.g. a public IPv6 prefix or VPN networks, one per line.
settings.allow_nets_public: Public networks entered ({nets}): DNS64 answers every device in them, strangers too. Only enter what really belongs to you, and never forward port 53/853 on your router.
settings.refused: {n} queries from foreign addresses refused since start, last {ip} ({time}).
settings.up_hint: Queries to the internet go encrypted to the ticked servers: DoH (HTTPS, port 443), DoT (TLS, port 853) or DoQ (QUIC, port 853). Each server's certificate is verified.
settings.up_mode_hint: Fastest: only asks the fastest servers, the others step in on failure. Parallel: every query to all. In order: the next one only on error.
settings.up_add_hint: Unencrypted just the IP (e.g. 8.8.8.8). Encrypted: https://…/dns-query (DoH), tls://name (DoT), quic://name (DoQ) – with a name in the address bootstrap IPs are required.
settings.notify_upstream: Upstream server failing for more than 3 minutes and back again
settings.notify_lists: Blocklist failed to load three times in a row
settings.notify_hint: Sent to the default channels (not during quiet hours), set up under
settings.up_plain_title: Classic DNS over port 53: queries leave unencrypted.

setup.router: Enter this host's IP as DNS server in your router (DHCP). Then all devices on your network use DNS64 automatically.

setup.later: Encrypted queries from devices (DoH/DoT/DoQ) are on the “Encryption” tab.

js.rec_hint_TXT: Any text, e.g. for verifications or SPF.

js.rec_hint_CAA: Flag, issue/issuewild/iodef and value, e.g. 0 issue letsencrypt.org.

js.empty_chart: No queries in this time range yet
js.flush_confirm: Flush the cache? The next queries go to the upstream servers again.
js.reason_nodata: NODATA – name exists, but no record of this type

records.rel_hint: Name relative to the zone, @ = the zone itself, with a trailing dot = full name
records.local_only: This node only (not synced in the cluster)
records.comment_ph: optional, e.g. NAS in the basement
records.no_ptr: No reverse lookup (PTR) from this record
records.import_hint: Hosts file (IP and names per line), CSV (name,type,value,ttl,comment) or JSON. Existing records stay, localhost and 0.0.0.0 lines are skipped.
records.title: Custom DNS records
records.hint: *.home.lan applies to all names below; A/AAAA get the reverse lookup too. Custom records take precedence over blocklists and never go to the internet.

hint.note: {host} is not reachable right now. This page is shown by Node64 (DNS64).

groups.schedules_hint: In the node’s time zone; end before start = over midnight. “Internet off”: only local names and the group’s allowed domains. “Free” suspends schedules and categories for a while.
groups.safesearch_hint: Searches only with SafeSearch, YouTube in restricted mode; cannot be switched off on the device. YouTube “off” = YouTube without restriction (block it with the streaming category).
groups.bypass_hint: Blocks foreign DoH servers, VPNs and proxies plus iCloud Private Relay and Firefox’s DoH. A device can still get around it via mobile data.
groups.hint_rules: Each group has its own rules (under “Rules”). Devices without a group use the settings under “Blocklists”.
groups.cats_hint: Small curated lists (e.g. TikTok, Roblox, Netflix); gambling and adult content via HaGeZi. An allowed domain of the group always takes precedence.
groups.domains_hint: Applies with subdomains. A release beats blocks, categories and blocklists, e.g. the school platform.
groups.title: Groups
groups.hint: Groups bundle devices, e.g. “Kids” or “Guests”. A device belongs to at most one group; if it matches several (e.g. by MAC and by network), the upper one wins.
groups.hint_mac: Devices are recognised by MAC first and so keep their group even with a new IP. DNS64 only sees the MAC on the same network – otherwise enter an IP or network.
groups.label: Label

logs.title: Log sensor and syslog
logs.intro: Reads logs of real services (SSH, web servers, mail …) and accepts syslog from routers. Attacks only count above a threshold, e.g. 5 failed logins in 10 minutes.
logs.privacy: From real logs only IP, kind, service, port, count and rule are stored and reported – no user names, passwords, paths, user agents or other content.

healthchecks.desc: Monitors websites, servers and services locally in your home network and optionally online from ipv64 – with notifications on outages and recovery.

healthchecks.h2: Status pages, maintenance windows and many notification channels

dyndns.h1: IPv4 and IPv6, including prefixes for devices in your network
dyndns.h2: Reports failed updates and IP changes

cdn64.desc: Reverse proxy for the services in your home network: names with HTTPS certificates, access protection and forwarding – locally or via the ipv64 CDN64 servers.
cdn64.h1: Automatic certificates, country blocking, blocklists and access protection
cdn64.h2: Reachable even without open ports via the CDN64 servers

dns64.h1: Blocklists, device groups with schedules and SafeSearch
dns64.h2: DNS over TLS, HTTPS and QUIC, own records and zones

honeypot.desc: A decoy in your network: detects attackers trying credentials and reports them to the IPv64 blocklists.
honeypot.h1: Simulates common services such as SSH, Telnet and web logins
honeypot.h2: Early warning and a contribution to the shared blocklists

sonar64.desc: Community measurement network: your node sparingly measures latency to other participants and the anchors, following a signed plan from ipv64 – visible on the map at ipv64.net/sonar.
sonar64.h1: Ping via ICMP and UDP 6464, fixed limits, never private targets
sonar64.h2: Outgoing only or also measured, location only shown blurred

monitor64.desc: Monitors your systems with thresholds and history: fill levels, CPU, RAM, disks with SMART, network and bonding – via agent, SSH, SNMP or API.

monitor64.h2: Problems with history, maintenance and notifications – all local

sonar64.title: Sonar64
sonar64.intro: Community measurement network: nodes measure each other and ipv64’s anchors – sparingly and within fixed limits. Results on ipv64.net/sonar.

participate.title: Participation
participate.text: By participating, this node becomes a Sonar64 node. It measures response times to other nodes and to the anchors and reports them, signed, to ipv64 every 5 minutes.
participate.p1: Targets only come from the signed plan from ipv64, never private networks; a few packets per second, fixed daily limit.
participate.p2: Public are display name, provider, access type, trust level and the location blurred to about 1 km – never your IP address.
participate.p3: The default is "outbound only": others only measure you once you choose "also measured".
participate.nokey: To participate, Node64 needs the central ipv64 API key (a dedicated Sonar token is created from it).
participate.off_confirm: Leave Sonar64? The node signs off its Sonar64 node at ipv64.net, stops measuring and no longer answers on UDP 6464. Participating again later creates a new node.

revoked.title: Signed off by ipv64.net
revoked.text: ipv64.net has deregistered this node. The node no longer measures and checks hourly whether this was lifted.
revoked.rejoin_hint: Creates a new Sonar token and a new node (new node ID, the trust level starts over).
revoked.rejoin_confirm: Participate in Sonar64 again with a new node?

new.intro: What do you want to monitor? You can add further access methods later (e.g. Proxmox via API plus SSH for bonding and temperatures).
new.agent_step1: 1. Install the agent on the host

new.ssh_key: Add this key on the host
new.ssh_safe: Only from this node, without forwarding. Each round runs a fixed, read-only script. Recommended: a dedicated user “monitor64”.
new.smart: Read SMART values (needs this line in sudoers, e.g. via visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/monitor64)
new.pw_auth: Password instead of key – only for systems that do not accept keys
new.token_cmd: Create a read-only token (run on the server)

new.node: Node name (empty = the node behind the address, fixed on first contact)
new.pin: Pin fingerprint (certificate SHA-256 or SSH host key, optional)
new.docker_hint: Local: unix:///var/run/docker.sock (mount the socket into the Node64 container). Remote: tcp://host:2375, https://host:2376 with TLS or ssh://user@host. Podman: enable podman.socket (systemctl enable --now podman.socket), then unix:///run/podman/podman.sock or ssh://user@host/run/podman/podman.sock.
new.test_ok: connected – {n} services found, answer in {ms} ms
new.no_test: Not tested yet – services are discovered after creation and offered for adoption.
new.found: Found: {n} services. Untick what you don't need – default thresholds are already set.
new.tags_hint: Tags can have their own thresholds, e.g. “backup”: storage only from 95 %.
new.cluster_nodes: Add further nodes of cluster {c} as separate hosts
new.cluster_hint: One host per node with the same token, queried via the same address. This host then shows only its own node.
new.summary_nodes: Plus {n} further node(s) as separate hosts.
new.fp_confirm: Certificate or host key is not confirmed yet – token or password were not sent. Compare the fingerprint with the server and confirm it.
new.smart_hint: Allows only the calls the script needs (find disks, read values without waking sleeping disks). If smartctl lives elsewhere, adjust the path (command -v smartctl).
new.hint_prom: Exporter address, e.g. http://10.0.0.5:9100/metrics (node_exporter) or port 9182 (windows_exporter). Empty: host address, port 9100.
new.hint_nut: Address of upsd (port 3493). Set "LISTEN <IP> 3493" in upsd.conf. Reading needs no login; user and password from upsd.users only if wanted. Encrypted via STARTTLS if upsd has a certificate.
new.hint_truenas: Under Settings → Users create a user with the role "Read-Only Administrator" and an API key for it; enter the user name as well (required from TrueNAS 27). https:// only – TrueNAS revokes keys used over http://.
new.hint_unraid: Under Settings → Management Access → API Keys create a key with the role "Viewer" (built in from Unraid 7.2, before that plugin "Unraid Connect"). https:// recommended.
new.hint_redfish: Create a separate BMC user with the role "ReadOnly" (iDRAC: Read Only, iLO: Login, Supermicro: User). The certificate is usually self-signed – confirm the fingerprint during the test.
new.hint_snmp: Enable SNMP on the device (read-only) and allow this node as a manager. Preferably v3 with authentication and privacy; v1/v2c send the community in clear text. The node picks profiles (Synology, QNAP, MikroTik, UniFi, APC, printers …) itself.
new.unconfirmed: The host's fingerprint is not confirmed yet. You can still create the host – but the password is only sent after you compared and confirmed the fingerprint via "Test" at the access. Better: go back to step 2 and confirm it there.
new.hint_pmg: In the Mail Gateway under Configuration → User Management, create a dedicated user with the role "Auditor" (realm "Proxmox Mail Gateway Authentication Server", without a second factor) and enter it here with its realm, e.g. monitor64@pmg. The Mail Gateway has no API tokens, hence user and password. The certificate is usually self-signed – confirm the fingerprint during the test.
new.hint_mailcow: In mailcow under System → Configuration → Access → API, enable read-only access, add this node's address to "Allow API access from" and paste the key here. Note: mailcow counts requests with a wrong key as failed logins and may ban the node (Fail2ban).
new.hint_fritzbox: In the FRITZ!Box enable "Allow access for applications" under Home Network → Network → Network Settings and create a dedicated user under System → FRITZ!Box Users. For all values it needs the right "FRITZ!Box Settings" – the FRITZ!Box has no read-only role; without the right you get access type, line state and the update status. Access works from the home network only. The certificate is self-signed – confirm the fingerprint during the test.

nf.where_hint: The all-clear goes exactly to the channels that received the problem. “Unreachable” counts as critical. Channels are set up under Notifications – the same as for health checks.
nf.default_sub: all channels marked as default in Node64
nf.when1: Every deterioration (OK → warning → critical) and the all-clear. Critical → warning arrives as “better, but still warning”.
nf.when2: Everything that happens on one host in one round is one notification. Many hosts at once: the digest from the Node64 settings.
nf.when3: Host unreachable: one notification – not one per service. Back again: one notification with what is still open.
nf.when4: If a service flaps (more than 5 changes in 30 min): one notification, then silence until it is stable for 30 min.
nf.when5: Never: “display only”, maintenance (afterwards only what is still open), acknowledged (until it gets worse), new services (hint only).
nf.remind: Remind while open and not acknowledged
nf.quiet_from_settings: from the Node64 settings (like health checks)
nf.quiet_text: Nothing is sent during quiet hours. Afterwards each channel gets one digest: what happened and what is still open.
nf.crit_in_quiet: Notify critical immediately even during quiet hours
nf.no_crit_in_quiet: Hold back critical during quiet hours
nf.overrides_hint: Like the thresholds: one list, the upper one wins.

agent.title: Monitor64 agent
agent.intro: The Monitor64 agent delivers the values of Linux, Windows and FreeBSD. This node fetches the signed files, verifies them and keeps them ready – also for hosts without internet access – and updates installed agents over the existing connection.
agent.cmd: Run on the host (as root, or in a PowerShell as administrator)
agent.node_key_hint: The agent only accepts requests made with this key; it is part of the install command. Fingerprint:
agent.node_addr: Address of this node as the host reaches it
agent.hint_net: Script and file come from {h} over HTTPS. The script checks the file against SHA256SUMS from the same folder: that protects against broken downloads – against tampering, only HTTPS protects on this path.
agent.hint_node_https: Script and file come from this node over HTTPS; it only serves files whose signature it has verified. The host must trust the node's certificate: with a self-signed certificate the download fails (curl and PowerShell verify the certificate). In that case enter the HTTP address (e.g. {u}) or choose the source Internet.
agent.hint_node_https_only: Script and file come from this node over HTTPS; it only serves files whose signature it has verified. The host must trust the node's certificate: with a self-signed certificate the download fails (curl and PowerShell verify the certificate). In that case set up a valid certificate or choose the source Internet.
agent.hint_node_http: Warning, HTTP is unprotected: anyone on the network between host and node can replace script and file. The checksum travels the same way – it only protects against broken downloads, not against tampering, and the agent runs as root. Use it only in your own trusted network; otherwise use HTTPS with a valid certificate or the source Internet.
agent.none: The node has not loaded the agent files yet.
agent.src_stored: Taken from the node's own store – not checked again since the start.
agent.src_from: Sources: {s}. The signature is verified with the Node64 release key.

agent.err_no_index: Agent files not available (source unreachable or signature invalid)
agent.err_no_file: there is no agent file for {platform}

note.counters_unreadable: reliability counters not readable (administrator rights needed?)

txt.addr_no_path: invalid address "{addr}" (enter it without a path)
txt.apikey_rejected: API key rejected (revoked, expired or wrong?)
txt.cert_changed: Certificate mismatch – fingerprint {fp} instead of the stored one (confirm the new certificate?)
txt.cred_newline: user and password must not contain line breaks
txt.docker_addr_invalid: invalid Docker address "{addr}" (unix://, tcp://, http(s):// or ssh://)
txt.http_plain: unencrypted (http://) – credentials cross the network in clear text, https:// recommended
txt.node_unknown: Node not detected (cluster/status has no local node) – enter the node name
txt.nut_access_denied: access denied – check LISTEN/ACL in upsd.conf and the user
txt.nut_cert_unconfirmed: upsd certificate not confirmed – confirm fingerprint {fp} in the access settings
txt.nut_data_stale: no current data from the driver
txt.nut_plain_nologin: unencrypted (upsd without STARTTLS) – login skipped so the password does not cross the network in clear text (not needed for reading)
txt.nut_plain_password: the password is sent to upsd unencrypted (no STARTTLS) – upsd needs no login for reading
txt.nut_tls_gone: upsd used TLS so far; if it no longer offers TLS, switch TLS off in the access settings
txt.pin_mismatch: fingerprint {fp} does not match the pin
txt.pm_auth: login rejected – check user/password or token
txt.pm_cred_chars: user or password/token contains invalid characters
txt.pm_cred_in_url: do not put credentials into the address (user and password or token belong in the credentials)
txt.pm_custom_label_bad: custom metric "{name}": label too long or empty
txt.pm_custom_name_bad: custom metric "{name}": invalid name (allowed: a-z, A-Z, 0-9, _ and :)
txt.pm_custom_name_n: custom metric {n}: name missing or too long
txt.pm_custom_none: none of the custom metrics found
txt.pm_custom_title_long: custom metric "{name}": display name or unit too long
txt.pm_no_metrics: no Prometheus metrics in the response – check address/path (default /metrics)
txt.pm_pin_mismatch: certificate changed – fingerprint does not match the stored one
txt.pm_protobuf: response in protobuf format – only the text format is supported
txt.pm_redirect: redirects are not followed, enter the address directly
txt.pm_unconfirmed: certificate not confirmed – check and accept the fingerprint
txt.rf_hint_perm: the user needs at least the ReadOnly role
txt.snmp_auth_short: v3 password (authentication) too short (at least 8 characters)
txt.snmp_no_system: no reply to the system group
txt.snmp_priv_short: v3 password (privacy) too short (at least 8 characters)
txt.snmp_table_loop: too many requests for one table
txt.snmp_warn_community: community is sent unencrypted – v3 recommended
txt.tn_hint_auth: check the API key (revoked? TrueNAS revokes keys that were used over http://)
txt.tn_hint_perm: the API key needs read access (user with the role Read-Only Administrator)
txt.tn_https_only: TrueNAS only via https:// (TrueNAS revokes API keys used over http://)
txt.tn_login_gone: auth.login_with_api_key no longer exists (TrueNAS 27) – enter the user of the API key
txt.tn_rest_deprecated: the REST API is deprecated since TrueNAS 25.04 – choose JSON-RPC
txt.tn_rpc_missing: JSON-RPC (wss://…/api/current) not available – TrueNAS before 25.04: choose REST
txt.tn_user_needed: enter the user of the API key – login without a user is removed in TrueNAS 27
txt.ur_hint_absent: no Unraid API at /graphql (built in since Unraid 7.2, before that the Unraid Connect plugin)
txt.ur_hint_auth: check the API key (Settings → Management Access → API Keys)
txt.ur_hint_perm: the API key needs the Viewer role
txt.updates_forbidden: not queried – the token lacks the permission (Proxmox VE: Sys.Modify on /nodes, the PVEAuditor role is not enough)
txt.pmg_tfa: the user has a second factor – create a user without a second factor for monitoring
txt.pmg_hint_auth: check the user with realm (e.g. monitor64@pmg) and the password
txt.pmg_hint_perm: the user lacks the role Auditor
txt.pmg_role_admin: the user is an administrator – the role Auditor is enough for monitoring
txt.mailflow: last hour: {in} in, {out} out, {spam} spam, {virus} viruses, {rej} rejected
txt.clamav_old: ClamAV signatures not updated for {n} days
txt.mc_hint_auth: check the API key and add this node's address to "Allow API access from" in mailcow
txt.pi_undervolt: under-voltage – check power supply and cable
txt.fb_user_missing: user missing (FRITZ!Box user, without quotes and colon)
txt.fb_hint_auth: check the FRITZ!Box user and password
txt.fb_hint_perm: the user lacks the right "FRITZ!Box Settings" – without it connection, DSL values and uptime are missing
txt.fb_no_tr064: no TR-064 description – enable "Allow access for applications" in the FRITZ!Box, port 49443
txt.fb_no_service: the FRITZ!Box does not offer this service
txt.fb_too_many: too many rejected logins – the FRITZ!Box blocks temporarily
txt.fb_dsl: sync {d} down / {u} up · noise margin {sd} / {su} dB
